text: Don't forget the answer key at the end of quizzes — every time.
Sign it 'Dr. R' like always; never use my full name with students.
No extra credit, ever. Don't offer it.
Student replies should stay short, around 120 words at most, unless I say so.
Use students' first names when you write to them.
Dates go weekday first, no year: 'Thursday, Oct 15'.
All math in quiz drafts in LaTeX, please, fractions too.
Again: no 'all of the above' or 'none of the above' choices.
I don't answer student email on weekends, so no promises of a weekend reply.
One draft, not a menu of options.
140 quizzes run fifteen minutes.
No graphing calculators in MATH 140 — scientific or four-function only.
142 exams are entirely free response; there's no bubble sheet.
In 142, write derivatives as dy/dx, not with primes.
The coordinator writes the 140 exams, so you only ever draft quizzes for that course.
My 140 TA does the quiz grading this semester; exams are mine.
Regrades for 140 this term go through Gradescope, not email.
142 worksheet groups are fixed threes this semester.
Extensions need a doctor's note. No note, no extension.
One reminder for missing work is enough; don't keep after them.

recent: How many versions should Quiz 5 have?
text: Three from now on, not four. That's for every quiz.
say: Make three versions of every quiz.

text: Actually, let student replies run up to 200 words; 120 was too tight.
say: Keep student replies under about 200 words unless asked for more.

text: Sign student emails 'Professor R' from now on instead of 'Dr. R'.
say: Sign student emails 'Professor R', never the full name.

text: I've changed my mind on dates: put the date first, then the weekday in parentheses — 'Oct 15 (Thursday)'.
say: Write dates with the date first and the weekday in parentheses, like 'Oct 15 (Thursday)'.

text: Rubric partial credit can now go in quarter-point steps; half points were too coarse.
say: Rubric partial credit uses quarter-point steps.

text: Start addressing students as Mr. or Ms. Lastname in emails; first names felt too casual.
say: Address students as Mr. or Ms. Lastname in emails.

text: Tables should be sorted by UIN from now on, not last name.
say: Sort tables by UIN unless told otherwise.

text: Put the point value at the end of each question in parentheses instead of at the start in brackets.
say: Show each question's point value in parentheses at the end of the question.

recent: That subject line is too clipped.
text: Let them run up to twelve words from now on.
say: Keep email subject lines under twelve words.

text: New rule for quizzes: order the questions the way the topics were taught, not by difficulty.
say: Order quiz questions by the order the topics were taught.

text: MATH 140 quizzes are 20 minutes now, not 15 — that's permanent for the course.
say: MATH 140 quizzes are 20 minutes long.

text: 142 quizzes should be 25 minutes going forward.
say: MATH 142 quizzes are 25 minutes long.

text: No more formula sheet on 140 quizzes — fully closed-book in this course from now on.
say: MATH 140 quizzes are fully closed-book, with no formula sheet.

text: In 140, probability answers should be decimals to four places, not fractions.
say: MATH 140 probability answers are decimals to four places.

text: For 142, write original quiz questions; stop pulling from the suggested homework list.
say: MATH 142 quiz questions are written fresh, not taken from the suggested homework list.

text: Change for the rest of this term: 140 quizzes move online in Canvas.
say: This term MATH 140 quizzes are online in Canvas.

text: For 142 this fall I'll post worked solutions a week after each quiz, not the next morning.
say: This term MATH 142 worked solutions are posted a week after each quiz.

recent: Where do the 140 makeups happen again?
text: With the TA after all this term, not in my office hours.
say: This term a missed MATH 140 quiz is made up with the TA.

text: Tell students quiz scores come back within two weeks, not one.
say: Tell students quiz scores come back within two weeks.

text: I've decided to curve 140 quizzes this semester after all.
say: This term MATH 140 quizzes are curved.

text: In MATH 142, quizzes only need two versions — the class is small.
say: MATH 142 quizzes need only two versions.

text: For worksheets, skip the answer key — that's only for quizzes.
say: Worksheet drafts do not get an answer key.

text: Replies to my TA can be as long as needed; the word limit is only for students.
say: Replies to the TA have no word limit.

text: On the 140 finance unit only, students may use a financial calculator.
say: On the MATH 140 finance unit only, students may use a financial calculator.

text: During finals week I do answer student email on Saturday.
say: During finals week the instructor answers student email on Saturday.

text: Regrade requests for the 140 final this term come by email, since Gradescope closes.
say: This term regrade requests for the MATH 140 final come by email.
